git_basics.notes: Maintained expert level. Applied Git fundamentals throughout PR workflow: pushing branches with upstream tracking, reviewing diffs, merging via GitHub interface, cleaning up local and remote branches post-merge.

terminal_comfort.notes: Maintained proficient level. Executed multi-step terminal workflows: git push -u, git checkout, git pull, git branch -d. Comfortable with command sequences for PR workflow.

markdown_documentation.notes: Updated from previous practice. Created structured PR descriptions using markdown formatting. Documented workflow in README with proper headers, lists, and code formatting.

project_organization.notes: Maintained competent level. Applied branching workflow to organize features. Successfully completed full GitHub Flow cycle (branch → commit → push → PR → review → merge → delete).

technical_vocabulary.notes: Maintained proficient level. Expanded vocabulary with PR and GitHub concepts: pull request, base branch, compare branch, PR description, draft PR, status checks, GitHub Flow, code review, merge button, PR diff, upstream tracking, issue linking, merge commit.

systems_thinking.notes: Maintained proficient level. Demonstrated understanding of how PR workflow creates compound value over time. Recognition that documentation serves multiple purposes (review, portfolio, future reference, collaboration). Meta-awareness of 'unknown unknowns' shows advanced self-reflection.

commit_message_writing.notes: Maintained expert level. Applied Conventional Commits format to PR titles. Understanding of merge commit message conventions and when to use defaults vs customization.

github_workflow.notes: Advanced from proficient to expert. Successfully executed complete GitHub Flow cycle. Created issue, opened PR with professional description, linked issue with 'Closes #N', reviewed diff, merged, deleted branch. Textbook-perfect first PR execution.

ssh_authentication.notes: Already had SSH configured from previous work (The Odin Project, dev-curriculum). Excellent understanding of ssh-agent purpose, SSH vs HTTPS tradeoffs, and Personal Access Token distinctions. Professional-level authentication setup. Ready for advanced scenarios (multiple SSH keys, SSH config management).

remote_repository_management.notes: Advanced from proficient to expert. Complete mastery of remote branch workflows: pushing with upstream tracking (git push -u), fetching PR merges (git pull), deleting remote branches via GitHub UI, cleaning up local branches post-merge. Understanding of origin/main vs local main distinction.

multi_device_sync.notes: Excellent visualization of two-computer workflow (pull → work → commit → push → repeat). Understands importance of pulling before starting work to avoid conflicts. Ready for real-world multi-device CatchBook development scenarios.

atomic_commits.notes: Maintained expert level. Applied atomic commit principles in feature branch and PR context. Understanding that PRs aggregate atomic commits into logical feature units.

git_history_navigation.notes: Maintained expert level. Understanding of how merge commits appear in git log and how to trace feature development through PR history on GitHub.

gitignore_configuration.notes: Proactively created .gitignore during L02 bonus challenge, enhanced with comprehensive patterns in L04. Understands why files should be ignored (secrets, dependencies, build artifacts, OS files, IDE configs). Correct pattern syntax knowledge. Excellent understanding of git rm --cached for retroactive exclusion. Strong security awareness—immediately recognized API key prevention as critical use case. Portfolio-ready repository hygiene.

security_awareness.notes: Maintained competent level. Applied security thinking to PR review: checking diffs for secrets, understanding importance of reviewing changes before merge.

git_branching.notes: Maintained expert level. Successfully completed full branch lifecycle: create → commit → push → PR → merge → delete. Understanding of branch cleanup importance for repository hygiene.

command_line_fluency.notes: Maintained proficient level. Executed multi-step workflows combining Git commands, GitHub web interface actions, and local repository cleanup.

professional_workflow_patterns.notes: Advanced from competent to proficient. Demonstrated professional-grade PR execution: Conventional Commits title, structured description (What/Why/Changes/Testing/Notes), issue linking, metadata (labels, assignees), clean diff review. Ready to apply this pattern across 140+ future modules.

pull_request_workflow.notes: NEW SKILL. Exceptional first-time PR execution. Complete understanding of PR as communication tool (not just merge mechanism). Mastery of GitHub Flow 6 steps. Created PR #1 with professional description structure, proper issue linking, clean diff, appropriate metadata. Understanding of PR value for documentation, portfolio presentation, and long-term project navigation. Recognized 'Why' section as most valuable for preserving architectural decisions. Successfully adapted to GitHub UI changes independently.

github_issue_management.notes: NEW SKILL. Created first GitHub issue with acceptance criteria. Understanding of issue/PR linking system as 'breadcrumbs' for navigating project history. Demonstrated ability to write clear issue descriptions. Understanding of how issues + PRs create complete development history for complex projects. Ready for advanced issue management (milestones, projects, templates).

pr_description_writing.notes: NEW SKILL. Excellent PR description structure following What/Why/Changes/Testing/Notes template. Understanding that 'Why' section documents reasoning not recoverable from code. Recognition of PR descriptions as documentation for future-self, collaborators, and portfolio presentation. Self-awareness of 'unknown unknowns' demonstrates healthy learning mindset.

diff_review.notes: NEW SKILL. Understanding of diff view mechanics (green additions, red deletions, line counts). Correct identification of line ending differences as potential cause of discrepancies. Awareness of other causes (blank lines, formatting, markdown artifacts). Understanding importance of reviewing diffs before merge to catch unintended changes. Ready for more complex diff scenarios (conflicts, large changesets).

issue_pr_linking.notes: NEW SKILL. Complete understanding of 'Closes #N' syntax for automatic issue closure on PR merge. Recognition of bidirectional linking value (issue → PR, PR → issue). Demonstrated understanding of how linking system enables future navigation and debugging. Excellent 'breadcrumbs' analogy for explaining traceability. Understanding of GitHub search capabilities for finding historical context.
